questions.text: What does a health factor of 0.9 mean?
options: Your position is very safe
Your position can be liquidated
You need to deposit more collateral to borrow
Your interest rate is 0.9%

questions.text: If the max LTV is 75% and you borrow at 60% LTV, are you safe?
options: No, you're over the limit
Yes, but with limited buffer against price drops
Yes, with a comfortable safety margin
It depends only on the interest rate

questions.text: Why is Supply APY lower than Borrow APY?
options: It's a bug in the protocol
The protocol takes a spread for reserves and revenue
Suppliers take more risk
Borrowers get a discount

questions.text: What is the liquidation penalty for?
options: Punishing the borrower
Incentivizing liquidators to repay bad debt at a discount
Paying gas fees
Funding the DAO treasury

questions.text: You deposit $10,000 of ETH (LT 82.5%) and borrow $5,000 USDC. What is your starting health factor?
Your ETH collateral drops 30% in a flash crash. Your HF was 1.5 before. What's the smart move?
options: Wait — it'll bounce back
Take out more loans to average down
Repay part of your debt or add collateral immediately
Switch to a stable interest rate

questions.text: When would you choose a stable rate over a variable rate?
options: When you expect rates to drop sharply
For very short-term loans
For long-term loans where you want predictable interest
When the variable rate is higher than the stable rate
